reads: window.sessionStorage access token and auth user
writes: sessionStorage access token and auth user
contracts: server-only JWT verification and RBAC CLI-506/702
security_boundaries: refresh token intended to remain in httpOnly cookie
access token remains in memory/sessionStorage and server verification is authoritative
server revocation is attempted before local logout
tenant_boundaries: identity changes compare userId and orgId before emitting AuthChange
session user carries orgId but authorization is server-enforced
failure_paths: disabled or exceptional Storage leaves memory usable
malformed session user falls back to token-derived display identity
server logout failure does not prevent local cleanup
tests: cross-tab session security tests and AppContainer lifecycle consumers

findings.evidence: The short-lived access token and UI user are stored in sessionStorage.
findings.impact: XSS in the application can read the access token within a tab; the design trades this residual exposure against refresh UX while server authorization remains authoritative.
findings.fix: Keep the token memory-only if refresh-page behavior permits, and continue CSP/XSS hardening.

findings.evidence: Cached session AuthUser validates only roles and username, not canonical userId/orgId syntax.
findings.impact: Corrupt display identity may render incompletely; it cannot grant server authorization.
findings.fix: When touching identity contracts, validate canonical userId and nonempty orgId before caching display identity.

contracts: offset sign, five-minute skew boundary, and timestamp adjustment behavior
failure_paths: asserts positive/negative/zero offsets and skew tolerance
callers must provide valid numeric milliseconds; helpers perform no validation by design

contracts: 409 parsing, nested diff paths, and empty-server recommendation
failure_paths: covers non-conflict errors, missing serverValue, scalar/object diffs, and empty server recommendation

security_boundaries: unknown error shapes are rejected or ignored
failure_paths: recursive diff gracefully represents type mismatches

findings.evidence: diffValues uses recursive traversal without a depth limit.
findings.impact: A pathological deeply nested conflict payload may exhaust the client stack; normal bounded business payloads are unaffected.
findings.fix: If conflict payloads become externally large, add a maximum depth and render an explicit whole-value diff.

entry_points: offline pending action queue Jest suite
failure_paths: covers invalid JSON and unknown types/statuses, conflict/failure continuation, auto-skip with manual retry, and scoped retry without duplicates

reads: JSON pending-action array from injected StorageLike
writes: entire normalized pending-action array after append/update/remove/clear and each flush step
contracts: mobile pending action states and whitelist normalization
security_boundaries: unknown persisted types and statuses fail safe
missing secure UUID refuses duplicate-prone enqueue
tenant_boundaries: storage key is not identity namespaced; production caller uses identity-scoped IndexedDB and only migrates legacy storage
failure_paths: setItem failures propagate so callers cannot report false enqueue success
409 is marked conflict/non-retryable while other errors are retryable

findings.evidence: The localStorage implementation has one global key and no queue size cap.
findings.impact: It is only a legacy migration source in the current caller; as a general utility, a long offline period or multi-tab writes can exceed quota or race.
findings.fix: Retain it only as a migration adapter or add identity namespacing, quota reporting, and cross-tab coordination before reuse.

writes: mock toast and offline queue calls
contracts: offline enqueue success requires an actual queue write
enqueue failure must show explicit error
security_boundaries: offline path cannot be reported as queued when storage unavailable
failure_paths: covers successful queue and rejected queue path, asserting no false success toast
